neighbours.label: The word that introduces an alternative name for something (brand name, older spelling, short form, nickname, initials, 'known by a different name'), the slot just before the alias is given
fire: Ibuprofen is also sold under the brand name Advil in many pharmacies.
The town of Kingstown has an older spelling, Kingestoun, found in early maps.
Everyone in the band knew him only by his nickname, Smokey.
The Federal Bureau of Investigation is usually referred to by its initials, FBI.
Elizabeth is a long name, and her friends use the short form Liz.
The plant goes by the common name foxglove in most gardening books.
In German the country is known by a different name, Deutschland.
The disease was first described under the term dropsy by older doctors.
quiet: Ibuprofen is also sold in small bottles of fifty in many pharmacies.
The town of Kingstown has an older church, built in stone, near the river.
Everyone in the band knew him only as a quiet drummer from Ohio.
The Federal Bureau of Investigation is usually busy with cases across the country.
Elizabeth is a tall girl, and her friends play basketball with her.
The plant grows best in partial shade according to most gardening books.
In Germany the trains run on time in most large cities.
The disease was first described in detail by older doctors.

predictions: Naming nouns (name, spelling, form, nickname, initials) before an alias reach 0.4-0.8; the same frames without a naming noun stay under 0.1.
notes: Probe: 'brand names' 0.800, 'alternative spelling' 0.771, 'shorter form' 0.590, 'its name was later changed' 0.426, 'abbreviated form NATO' 0.397; same-topic sentences without a naming noun 0.026-0.030. The distinction is naming an entity by another label vs describing it.
